Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment: Acute onset (few days) of dry, itchy, red skin on arms and hands, starting after swimming. No prior skin disease, no systemic symptoms. Distribution limited to exposed areas. Patient reports high work stress but is otherwise well. 
- DDx and transcript align in suggesting irritant contact dermatitis (high likelihood) related to pool chemical exposure (chlorine). Allergic contact dermatitis is possible but less likely, given lack of spread and no prior atopic skin disease. Xerosis due to weather is possible (supported by patient concern), but acute onset and correlation with swimming are more consistent with irritant contact dermatitis.
- No conflicting information between transcript and DDx.

Management Plan
- Emollients recommended for dry skin.
- Topical steroid cream to reduce inflammation.
- Patient information leaflet about dermatitis provided.
- Over-the-counter antihistamines (Piriton, Loratadine) suggested for itchiness.
- Paracetamol and other painkillers not recommended.
- Advise symptomatic monitoring and to return for reassessment if no improvement in one week.
- management_plan_main_or_not_recorded: Main management as above; further interventions or referrals not discussed.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Irritant contact dermatitis – High likelihood. Sudden onset of symptoms after exposure to pool chemicals (chlorine) localized to exposed skin. No prior skin problems. 
- Allergic contact dermatitis – Moderate to low likelihood. Exposure to possible new allergen, but less likely due to distribution and lack of prior history.
- Xerosis due to dry weather – Low likelihood. Considered because patient suspects weather; however, time course points towards an irritant cause.
